ratings_why.fun: Phials that steep in hand make every turn a real hold-or-cast choice, and the board visibly grows from your brewing; the counting load keeps it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: Cards that ripen in your hand and small lens units that bounce spells onto big ones play unlike any of today's tribes, though a spell-count tribe is a familiar shape.

verdict_why: The v1 reading problems are fixed; what's left is one word on Almanac Seller, and more rounds would mostly make it different, not better.

points.text: Almanac Seller counts 'each spell you cast last turn', but The Alchymist's Echoes add to the Recipe without being cast. Say whether counted Echoes count here too.
The brewing fantasy reads well; the bluff and colour-change lore doesn't. An eyespot unit that fakes a big Phial in fights, or Old Carbonaria turning dark as the Recipe grows, would bring it in.
Lamplighter's 'what your biggest Phial would give it' makes the player do scaling math mid-read. Showing the number on the card in the shop would carry it.
Steep cap, Herald's cap, Recipe and multiples of 5 are a lot to hold at once; a Recipe counter and N badges on each Phial are a must for this to read at a glance.

standouts.why: Dame Pavonia never eats, so no spell can reach her and she lives on Echoes alone: the lore is the rule.
Mother Shipton leaves a smaller omen behind every big brew; simple to read and ties both builds together.
Burnet keeps the poison cabinet: your held Phials become damage, so holding pays in the fight you can see.

weakest.why: Lamp-Circler is a plain count-your-hand body with little moth in it.
Almanac Seller is a generic random-target buffer, and its count is the one unclear line left.
Lamplighter is the hardest card to read at a glance for a modest in-fight gain.

flags.note: Whether The Alchymist's counted Echoes count as spells cast last turn.
With Cocoon Spinner merging to a Phial 14 or 20, Burnet hits for that up to three times a fight.
Echoes scale on her own stats, so she compounds every turn; worth the owner's eye, not a cut.
